additional_info.subject: Case Description
additional_info.body:

Thank you in advance

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0413410-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP / R9 170002651] Cu logs check CRM:03098000097
additional_info.body:
Dear Filomena Carusone,
Thank you for reaching out and informing us about the issue that occurred yesterday, October 24th, with charger n. 170002651. We understand that the customer was unable to charge between 5:40 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. (Italy time) and that the cable remained blocked in the vehicle, which is undoubtedly a frustrating situation.
We want to assure you that we have already initiated our investigation to understand what might have happened.
As part of our initial analysis, we checked the charger logs for the mentioned period. According to our records, we identified the following CP (Control Pilot) value exchanges yesterday afternoon. Please note that the times in the logs are in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time):
@timestamp    @message
2025-10-24 18:08:17.900    2025-10-24T18:08:17.822261+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [DCC]  DC2: PilotState "E" --> "A"2025-10-24 18:07:30.519
2025-10-24T18:06:58.964318+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [DCC]  DC2: PilotState "A" --> "E"2025-10-24 18:01:46.845
2025-10-24T18:01:46.816676+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [DCC]  DC2: PilotState "A" --> "E"
Considering that Italy was on CEST (UTC+2) on that date, the times in the logs (between 18:01 and 18:08 UTC) would correspond approximately to 8:01 p.m. and 8:08 p.m. (20:01 and 20:08) in Italy time on October 24th.
Could you please confirm if this time period (around 8:00 p.m. in Italy) matches the exact moment when the customer encountered the issue with the charger? This confirmation is very important to help us accurately correlate the events.
We have already collected the complete logs, and our specialized team will analyze them as soon as possible in detail to identify the root cause of the blocked cable and the charging failure.
We greatly appreciate your patience and cooperation as we work to resolve this. We will keep you updated as soon as we have more information.
Thank you!
With best regards,
Guilherme Andre De Verissimo Dias
Siemens S.A.
SI E CS SD L3
201, Avenida 25 de Abril
2845-547, Corroios, Portugal

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0457734-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP / R9 170002651] Cu logs check CRM:03098000097
additional_info.body:
Buongiorno Filomena,
First of all, apologies for the confusion on the ticket number. The correct ticket number for this case is
ID0457734.
I analyzed the logs form the timestamp reported (between 17:30 and 18:00 UTC time), and these are my findings:
Customer attempted #3 times to charge with AC socket (ConnectorId:3)
2025-10-24T17:32:30.796317+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [ACC]  AC1: PilotState "A" --> "B1"
Charging fails due to already active error flags (initial value):
Since the error flags are reporting "initial value", I can assure that the AC socket was displayed as "out of order" on the HMI.
2025-10-24T17:34:30.387084+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [ACC]  AC1: Cable unplugged
2025-10-24T17:35:53.995493+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [ACC]  AC1: PilotState "A" --> "B1"
2025-10-24T17:35:54.492643+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [ACC]  AC1: charging cable locked
2025-10-24T17:35:54.637003+00:00 [FW070005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/1a6e2ddb9164[738]: outlet is out of order, no connect allowed
I do not see any "cable unplugegd" in the logs
2025-10-24T17:38:43.231559+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [ACC]  AC1: PilotState "A" --> "B1"
I do not see any "cable locked in the logs"
2025-10-24T17:38:43.453322+00:00 [FW070005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/1a6e2ddb9164[738]: outlet is out of order, no connect allowed
2025-10-24T17:52:24.431846+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [ACC]  AC1: try to unlock charging cable
2025-10-24T17:52:24.921851+00:00 [FW070005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4130] [ACC]  AC1: charging cable unlocked
Charger was rebooted from the Backend at 2025-10-24T18:01:44.700637+00:00 [FW070005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/1a6e2ddb9164[738]: OCPP: Received command: Reset (3836529) - {"type":"Hard"}
In conclusion:
The charging attempts failed as the customer attempted to charge on a "out of order" AC outlet.
Can you please confirm that the customer contacted you for issues on the AC charging?
From your opening message, I see that the customer mainly complained about the cable being stuck in the car. Since we are talking about AC charging, some considerations have to be made:
For AC charging, as per DC charging, the charger has no control on the locking of the cable in the EV. It is up to the EV to lock/unlock the cable
For AC charging, in opposition to DC charging, the charger locks the AC cable in the charger socket on the other hand of the cable.
Therefore, could you please clarify what the customer meant with "
cable was blocked in the car"?
From the logs, I can only assume that the customer complained about the AC cable being locked in the charger socket from
17:35:53 or
17:38:43 until 17:52:24. However, the cable was connected when the outlet was out of order, hence I cannot assure on the behavior of the locking mechanism of the AC socket when such wrong handling of the charging session happens.
The charger still presents the AC socket (ConnectorId:3) as out of order, due to the tripping of FC5 and/or FB1:
Once I will receive feedback from your side, I will forward the ticket to the Service colleagues from Italy in order to restore the AC socket on this charger.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
